title.narrative: Camp Coordination and Camp Management (CCCM) and Multi-purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) to potentially drought-affected populations in Oromia, Somali and South Ethiopia Regions.

description.narrative: IOM, with its partners, will provide one-time MPC assistance to 24,155 individuals (estimated 4,831 households), vulnerable agro-pastoralist households anticipated to be severely affected by drought conditions. The focus will be on empowering communities to prepare for and mitigate displacement risks, ultimately saving lives through coordinated action and providing anticipatory services. The overall objective is to pre-emptively take life-saving action to mitigate the worst impacts of the hazard before it occurs, minimizing the use of negative coping strategies and protecting the dignity and livelihoods of the affected populations. MPC will enable households to meet their basic needs without making critical choices between essential needs. Thereby preventing life-threatening situations.Under CCCM component, IOM partners will address two key pillars: community empowerment and information sharing. IOM partners will reach estimated 33,333 individuals (6,667 households) at risk of drought displacement. This will include working with community leaders to build and invest in community governance structures, such as community empowerment skills in negotiation, complaints and feedback mechanisms (CFM), and problem-solving. This will ensure that essential services are coordinated and accessible, service gaps are identified and addressed, and communities are equipped with real-time feedback mechanisms to resolve challenges. Regarding information sharing, a weekly Event Tracking Tool (ETT) will be deployed to capture information on the movement of livestock and herders. ETT data will provide information that informs humanitarian response and anticipatory actions. By utilizing ETT data, local authorities and partners will have the necessary information to identify potential displacement risks before they escalate and potentially mitigate. Data is collected through remote interviews with key informants, presented through dashboards and datasets, and released monthly to community leaders and partners (if mobility incidents are reported for the week). Basic information that is captured includes place of movement, place of origin, number of people moving, and reported priority needs.Anticipatory mechanisms will be strengthened through improved coordination with local authorities, community leaders and humanitarian actors. Regular coordination meetings will be held to ensure that the situation is well-known by all the local stakeholders service gaps are addressed proactively and communities are well-prepared. This initiative aims to strengthen anticipatory action and safeguard the well-being of those at risk by improving information management systems, enhancing referral mechanisms, and establishing community governance structures. Through these regular coordination meetings with humanitarian actors and government officials, community-led preparedness will be promoted, service gaps will be actively followed up on, and resilience to displacement risks will be improved in the targeted areas. The CCCM serves as an anticipatory mechanism to govern the displacement of pastoralist communities facing drought and ensure the grazing capacity and water availability is accessible to all in an organized way. It establishes inclusive governance structures, enhancing community capacity to proactively manage resources and coordinate services. This approach adapts to support vulnerable agro-pastoralists by fostering local ownership and engagement with authorities. Essential services include early warning systems, community consultations, and real-time feedback mechanisms to address challenges, ensuring resilience, saving lives, and minimizing tensions due to a competitive access to natural resources.
